job.title: Sales Manager SA and NT
job.description:
SA Sales Manager

$Competitive package inclusive of car allowance and annual bonus
﻿
Adelaide based | SA & NT Territory
Our client is a significant and well-regarded organisation in the Australian health sector. With a broad operational footprint and a strong commitment to clinical excellence, they are a trusted provider of healthcare services supporting doctors, specialists, hospitals, and patients across the country.


Who They Are
This organisation has built a strong reputation for patient focus and medical quality. Their culture values integrity, collaboration, and continuous improvement, and they are committed to empowering their people to drive meaningful outcomes. They are now seeking to appoint an SA Sales Manager — a newly created role — to bring dedicated sales leadership, structure, and performance discipline to their South Australian and Northern Territory operations.


The Role
Reporting to the SA Chief Executive Officer, the SA Sales Manager is a senior leadership position and a member of the SA Leadership Team. This is a newly created role that reflects the organisation’s commitment to building a structured, data-driven sales function capable of driving sustained growth across all referral markets — general practice, specialist, hospital, clinic, and commercial.

The SA Sales Manager will lead a team of four sales professionals covering South Australia and the Northern Territory. A key early priority will be implementing the sales operating framework, embedding KPI and pipeline disciplines, and using data to drive sales performance.

Year one outcomes will be measured against:
Achievement of business growth targets, sales and budgets for the State
Market share growth
Customer retention and satisfaction levels
Team performance and engagement outcomes

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Sales Leadership & Performance Management
Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing sales team across SA and NT
Establish sales objectives, KPIs, and performance expectations aligned with business goals
Monitor and analyse sales performance, providing regular feedback, 1:1 reviews, and development plans
Conduct regular field visits and joint customer calls with sales representatives
Drive accountability and a results-oriented sales culture

Sales Strategy & Business Development
Develop and mobilise the strategic plan and direction of the state sales function including business planning, operational planning, and budgets
Identify new business opportunities within hospitals, clinics, general practices, healthcare networks, and specialist practices
Manage strategic and high-value customer relationships and develop account growth plans for key customers
Expand market share through customer acquisition and retention strategies
Lead contract negotiations, business cases, and revenue enhancement initiatives

Market & Commercial Strategy
Analyse market trends, competitor activity, and industry developments across the SA and NT territories
Provide insights and recommendations to the SA CEO regarding service positioning and growth opportunities
Forecast sales performance and prepare budget recommendations
Assist with the development and execution of marketing concepts and strategies

CRM & Sales Capability
Lead or contribute to the evaluation, selection, and implementation of a CRM platform across the SA business
Establish CRM disciplines, pipeline management practices, and reporting frameworks
Leverage data and sales tools to drive pipeline accuracy, activity tracking, and conversion analysis

Quality, Risk & Compliance
Ensure compliance with legislative, regulatory, accreditation, and organisational policy requirements
Participate in risk identification, assessment, and planning activities
Actively contribute to quality improvement and continuous improvement initiatives


Your Profile
This is a leadership-first role. The primary mandate is to bring sales discipline, structure, and performance management capability to a team with genuine market potential. While healthcare or pathology sector experience is an advantage, the organisation is equally interested in highly disciplined sales leaders from adjacent sectors who can build performance frameworks and lift team capability.

Candidates may come from a range of backgrounds including:
•      Pharmaceuticals or medical devices
•      Healthcare services, hospital supply, or medical technology
•      Pathology, Radiology, diagnostics, or laboratory services
•      Other regulated or relationship-driven B2B sales environments

You will demonstrate:
•      Tertiary qualification in science, health, business, management, marketing, or a related discipline
•      8+ years’ experience in sales or territory management including B2B and B2C environments
•      8+ years’ experience successfully managing and leading sales teams to meet and exceed targets
•      A data-driven, KPI-focused approach to sales leadership with strong pipeline management and forecasting capability
•      Strong commercial acumen and strategic planning skills
•      CRM fluency and the demonstrated ability to implement or embed sales management systems
•      Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, and relationship-building skills
•      South Australian market knowledge and/or an existing network is preferred but not essential

Industry certification in a structured sales methodology (e.g. Miller Heiman, SPIN, Challenger, or equivalent) is highly regarded.

job.title: Anatomical Pathologist - NZ
job.description:
Anatomical Pathologist
Christchurch, New Zealand | Confidential Client
Our client — a leading pathology services provider — is seeking an Anatomical Pathologist to join its Christchurch laboratory. This is a genuine opportunity to shape laboratory practice, lead quality and process improvement, and deliver diagnostic excellence within a well-resourced, collaborative environment in one of New Zealand's most liveable cities.
The Role
You will take responsibility for overseeing key operational laboratory activities, including:
  • Coordinating and delivering scientific and technical training across the laboratory team.
  • Continuously reviewing and developing laboratory practices, and driving continuous process improvement.
  •  Ensuring adherence to operational standards, procedures, and quality frameworks.
  • Contributing a broad range of diagnostic skills relevant to the laboratory.
  • Investigating and resolving general and complex issues within the laboratory environment.
About You
  • Fully registered Medical Practitioner — Medical Council of New Zealand registration, or current AMC/AHPRA registration with eligibility to register in New Zealand.
  • Minimum 2 years' full-time clinical experience post-graduation (MBBS or equivalent).
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience delivering pathology services, with proficiency across Laboratory Information Systems, Patient Systems, Quality Control Systems, and Microsoft Office.
  • A sound basic knowledge of internal medicine and its clinical practices, and a strong grasp of the ethics of medical practice.
  • Customer-focused, with strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills — comfortable engaging with patients, relatives, clinicians, and laboratory staff, and confident in report writing and statistical evaluation of scientific data.
  • Proven initiative, problem-solving, and analytical ability, with the capacity to manage competing priorities and deliver to deadline — both autonomously and within a team.
  • Sound understanding of legislation, policies, and requirements impacting the laboratory environment, including quality improvement, work health and safety, privacy, and workplace diversity.
  • Willingness to undertake out-of-hours shift duties in line with safe-hours provisions, and a demonstrated commitment to ongoing formal and self-directed education.
Why Christchurch?
World-class lifestyle, easy commutes, the Southern Alps and Canterbury coastline on your doorstep — and a health sector investing heavily in pathology capability.
Apply in Confidence

job.title: Account Manager
job.description:

You are a highly organised, proactive, and relationship-focused professional who enjoys building strong connections, solving problems, and driving continuous improvement.   • Pathology, medical devices, diagnostics, or related health services

You will demonstrate:
  • Experience in account management, CRM management, or customer relationship roles

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills with a customer-centric, relationship-driven approach
  • Ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders and competing priorities across laboratory, operations, and business development teams
  • Strong organisational and administrative capabilities with excellent attention to detail
  • Proactive, solution-focused, and highly collaborative with a passion for continuous improvement

Experience within healthcare, pathology, medical devices, or related industries will be highly regarded.

Be part of a growing specialist pathology organisation with a reputation for clinical excellence and a genuine commitment to its people. You will work closely with senior leadership and business development teams, playing a significant role in enhancing customer experience and business growth. job.title: Regional Manager
job.description:
SunDoctors is Australia’s leading specialist skin cancer network, dedicated exclusively to the detection, diagnosis, and treatment of skin cancer. With over 350,000 patients seen each year and involvement in the diagnosis of almost 20% of all melanomas nationwide, SunDoctors is a purpose-driven organisation at the forefront of delivering life-saving care.
 
We are partnering with Predictus Search to appoint a Regional Manager — a pivotal operational leadership role accountable for the performance and growth of a network of SunDoctors clinics within an assigned region. This is a hands-on, high-impact position that blends commercial leadership with a genuine commitment to patient outcomes, clinical excellence, and team development.
 
This role offers the opportunity to lead an established network while also playing a key role in expansion, including the onboarding and integration of newly acquired clinics — ensuring consistent standards, strong culture alignment, and operational success from day one.
 
The Opportunity

  • Lead the financial and operational performance of clinics within your assigned region, taking ownership of the regional P&L including budgeting, forecasting, and performance optimisation.
  • Drive patient access and revenue growth through effective rostering, consulting room utilisation, and resource planning to meet demand across clinics.
  • Inspire, coach, and develop Practice Managers, building high-performing teams through structured onboarding, performance management, and succession planning.
  • Establish trusted, collaborative relationships with doctors across the region, acting as a key escalation point and partnering with recruitment teams to attract and retain top clinical talent.
  • Support network growth by leading the onboarding and integration of newly acquired clinics, ensuring seamless transitions, strong team engagement, and alignment with SunDoctors’ operating standards.
  • Champion exceptional patient experience, ensuring feedback and complaints are addressed promptly and that every clinic delivers consistently high-quality care.
  • Ensure clinics meet RACGP, ISO, and all relevant compliance and accreditation requirements, maintaining audit readiness and implementing continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Identify growth opportunities, strengthen referral pathways, and build strategic external partnerships to support regional expansion.
  • Promote and integrate Southern Sun Pathology services across clinics to enhance patient outcomes and service delivery.
 
About You

  • A proven leader with the ability to build, inspire, and develop high-performing clinical and administrative teams.
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience in healthcare, clinical services, or multi-site operational leadership.
  • Strong commercial acumen with demonstrated experience managing P&L, budgets, and financial performance.
  • Sound understanding of compliance and accreditation standards (RACGP, ISO, WHS).
  • A confident communicator with the ability to engage effectively with doctors, frontline teams, and senior stakeholders.
  • Highly organised and data-driven, with the ability to manage multiple priorities across geographically dispersed sites.
  • Passionate about healthcare, with a genuine commitment to patient safety, service excellence, and continuous improvement.
 
Why Join SunDoctors?

This is a unique opportunity to lead, influence, and grow a network of market-leading skin cancer clinics, while contributing to a mission that has a tangible impact on the health of Australians.
 
You will play a key role not only in operational excellence, but also in shaping the future footprint of the business through clinic expansion and acquisitions.
 
The role includes travel within the assigned region, with an expectation of being on-site across clinics approximately three to four days per week.

job.title: Clinical Veterinary Pathologist
job.description:
Full Time/Part Time/Remote Clinical Veterinary Pathologist 
                         
Gribbles Veterinary Pathology is a trading entity of Australian Clinical Labs and it is one of Australia’s leading Veterinary Pathology providers, with two dedicated veterinary laboratories within Australia. Each laboratory provides diagnostic pathology services for livestock, companion animal, university, and research veterinarians, as well zoo and wildlife organisations.
 
About the Opportunity
 
We are currently seeking an enthusiastic and dynamic Veterinary Clinical Pathologist with a client-oriented approach and excellent communication skills on a full-time or part-time basis, either 2-3 full days or a few hours each morning over 5 days.
 
In this role, you will provide timely diagnostic pathology services, including postmortem examinations, cytology, and haematology, and contribute to the provision of services and advice to a broad range of clients. The scope of pathology work at this laboratory is wide and is a true mix of both large and small animal pathology, and of both anatomical and clinical pathology.
 
Your Key Responsibilities
 
  • Interpretation of both anatomical (gross post mortem, histopathology) and clinical pathology results
  • This includes evaluation and interpretation of haematology, cytology, biochemistry, endocrinology, urinalysis, serology, microbiology & molecular results
  • Reviewing haematology and chemistry data, interpreting cytology, consulting on case management, liaising with clinicians
  • Provision of specialist advice and phone consultation to veterinary clients
  • Provide scientific leadership to the laboratory technical team through mentorship, audits, and assistance with laboratory electronic records management and reporting systems in accordance to NATA accreditation.
  • Provide support to the Commercial team to consistently understand and meet the needs of our clients and participation in marketing activities to meet professional expectations.
  • Cooperate and work well with others in pursuit of team goals
 
 
Essential requirements
 
  • Degree in Veterinary Science (BVSc) or equivalent.
  • Registration as a veterinarian with the Veterinary Practitioners Board in Australia.
  • Pathology qualification by examination, (e.g. ACVP, ECVP, MANZCVS) or equivalent diagnostic pathology experience in production animals.
  • Post Graduate qualification in veterinary pathology or related discipline is preferred.
  • Experience in clinical veterinary pathology is essential, and a demonstrated commitment to providing a high quality pathology service.
  • Quantitative analysis, data interpretation, cytology, clinical reasoning, correlating lab data with patient signs.
 
Our supportive professional environment also provides opportunities for further career development through continuing professional education development and active participation in continuing education seminars for clients.
 
Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications.

job.title: Head of Anatomical Pathology

Assist with budget preparation, monitoring of revenue, expenses, test volume, FTE utilization, report/result turnaround, as well as workflow, and customer/employee satisfaction; plan and manage technology innovations, new facility design and implementation, new business, laboratory expansion, focus on service, maintains compliance with State, Federal, CAP and other accreditation agencies' regulations, in adherence to departmental and company policies and procedures and promote the company's mission and values across the integrated laboratory network. Expected to participate in the Senior Leadership Team, coordinate AP Lab departments involved in initiatives, and help develop the strategic direction for the AP operations.
 
Key objectives:

Clinical oversight - Work across the geographical scope of the Laboratory, performing or supervising anatomical pathology services consistent with the pathologist’s scope of training and registration, and other diagnostic collection techniques, reporting cases, and conducting clinical meetings and case discussions.
Clinical Governance - Participate in all clinical governance activities, including clinical audit, clinical effectiveness, risk management, quality assurance and quality improvement activities.
Capacity building - Provide leadership to promote the interest and development of the unit through strategic planning, ensuring cohesion of the overall functions of the unit by working effectively with internal and external stakeholders while always maintaining positive interpersonal relationships.
Health and Safety and Infection Control - Ensure that all duties and responsibilities of this post are carried out in compliance with the local work health and safety requirements, but also to Australian standards.
 
Responsibilities

  • Collaborates with Anatomic Laboratory Director, Laboratory Medical Director, Laboratory Leadership, and other AP Laboratory staff to suggest test methodologies and instrumentation appropriate for clinical use.
  • Participate in the hiring, training, and promotion of laboratory staff in conjunction with Laboratory Leadership.
  • Grow and develop staff to increase overall knowledge base.
  • Create a culture of operational and continuous quality improvement.
  • Manages conflict and identifies problems to arrive at constructive solutions while maintaining positive working relationships.
  • Involved with the selection, validation, and implementation of new test platforms.
  • Oversees the technical and operational aspects of the Laboratory.
  • Supports the development and delivery of laboratory service collaterals.
  • Communicates to Management updates of departmental action items on a regular basis.
  • Ensures compliance with all applicable Federal, State, CAP, and other accreditation agencies' regulations.
  • Establishes and implements metrics, policies, objectives, and procedures for departments and reports on results and outcomes.
  • Ensures that CQI efforts in conjunction with the Quality Officer comply with regulatory and accreditation standards.
  • Coordinates, supports, and monitors laboratory departments with a major focus on improving the operations to run seamlessly to ensure quality patient care.
  • Assists in the development of budgets including recommendations for major equipment purchases.
  • Assists in the development of facility designs and remodels.
  • Develop and implement strategic plans in alignment with the company's values and mission.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

  • Candidates must have qualifications suitable for registration as a medical practitioner (such as a medical degree from an Australian institution)

  • Post-graduate speciality qualifications in general pathology, including anatomical pathology and microbiology, recognised by the Royal College of Pathologists (Australasia)
  • Anatomical/surgical pathologist is most preferred, but the clinical/general pathologist is considered as well.
  • Bachelor's Degree in Histotechnology, Cytotechnology, other science-related field, or equivalent; Master's degree preferred
  • HT/HTL, PA, CT ASCP certification required or equivalent.
  • 5 years experience in the laboratory, a similar environment
  • Three (3) or more years of supervisory experience, preferred.
  • Knowledge of Quality Improvement programs, processes, and tools
  • Ability to work with individuals at all organizational levels, particularly peers, team members, Pathologists, and other departments.

  • Prior experience validating and implementing new Excellent analytical, organizational, communication, interpersonal and public speaking Self-directed, open to new learning experiences and demonstrating teamwork.
